title: Self Collect Report for Chanel
description:
Requesting for Special Instruction | CHANEL (KUALA LUMPUR) SDN BHD.

The SC auto-report should be set up similarly to the BA & RD reports, where the email is sent to the merchant (Chanel) and Copy (CC) to CS at mysupport@dhl.com.
Upon receiving the report, the merchant (Chanel) can trigger the request to DHL CS by replying with the self-collection (SC) instruction.

It would be preferable for the SC instruction to come directly from Chanel to ensure they are informed of the request. Couriers are advised to guide and direct any SC requests from the consignee to Chanel.
-	If the consignee requests self-collection, the courier should inform them that shipments under Chanel require them to contact the merchant directly in order for the SC arrangement to be made.
-	The courier will then need to scan the shipment under self-collect so that it appears in the auto-report to the merchant.
Once the merchant receives the auto-report, they can liaise directly with the consignee to advise whether self-collection is possible and confirm the request. The merchant should then update DHLeC CS via email or the dedicated WhatsApp group so that the SC request can be raised in ODD. This ensures that all parties (Chanel, the consignee, and DHLeC) are aware of the request.

title: Data Loss in Splunk
description: Data loss affecting both MY and TH
notes:
Update from Tina under subjectemail: Production Issues: Splunk 

Hi all,

 

This is the closure summary of series of action taken to recover data lost due to disk storage full in Splunk farm happened in last Nov 2025.

 

Problem Statement:

Splunk indexers (where data stored) are running out of disk space – issue started from beginning of Nov 2025 when Splunk team have observed very high data load from other business services. As result the indexers started to purge the oldest data bucket from each server to make space for new incoming data.

 

Action taken to resolve storage issue in Splunk farm:

Immediate action taken via 2 change requests (RFC2089523 and RFC2093129) to increase to disk space from 10TB to 12TB per server, total of 100TB of new disk added into Splunk farm infrastructure on 20th Nov and 1st Dec 2025.

 

Action taken to recover data lost from 4 summary indexes below:

ecs_single_parcel_permanent

ecs_my_scnc

ecs_th_scnc_edd

ecs_th_scnc_sc_score

 

1) 7 service ticket requests logged for data bucket restoration from 45 Splunk indexers (PRG and CBJ).

2) The full backup used for data restoration dated on 17/18/19 of Oct 2025, this is the latest full backup copy prior the increase of disk used in Splunk farm. Buckets restored in 2 standalone test servers.

3) Splunk indexes are rebuilt in test servers after data restoration tasks are completed by Shift/backup team.

4) Data validation is conducted by DeC team.

 

Result of data validation:

1) Parcel volumes from Jan to May 2025 are reconciled closely.

2) Data from June to Sept 2025 does not reconcile, as the counts of encoded parcels versus what is available in the EDD and SCNC indexes do not align for both countries.

3) No further action/restoration can be done as the restoration has been completed and this represents the maximum data that could be recovered.

 

Preventive actions:

1) Implemented data volume based monitoring and alerting for sudden increase of data ingested per index in farm. Follow up action with service owner to rectify the issue/possible action to reduce the volume.

2) Continuous improvement action via PRB0198118 to improve the indexing rate of Splunk

title: New Dashboard
description:
The objective is to view a summary of the overall status based on the selected encoded date.
For example, when I filter the encoded date to 3rd February 2026, I should be able to see all shipments encoded on that date, along with a summary of their current overall status as of today.
Please explore this requirement and share any limitations or challenges you may encounter in developing this dashboard.
notes:
explain to alyu and adillah in email

"Dashboard Feasibility & Technical Challenges
                                                              i.      The dashboard requirement is straightforward in concept — filter by encoded date, see all shipments from that date, and view their current status. However, given our current data infrastructure, there are significant technical challenges we need to address before development.

 

The Core Problem: How Our Data is Stored in Splunk
                                                              i.      Splunk is an event-logging platform, not a transactional database. Every time a parcel's status changes — whether it's picked up, in transit, out for delivery, or delivered — a new row is written. This means a single parcel can generate anywhere from 5 to 20+ log entries throughout its journey.

                                                             ii.      With 1.6 million parcels per month, we're potentially dealing with 10 to 30+ million rows of data that need to be scanned and processed just to answer one simple question: "What is the latest status of each parcel encoded on this date?"

 

Specific Challenges
                                                              i.      Identifying the "latest" status per parcel is expensive

To show the current status of a parcel, we can't just pull all rows — we need to find the most recent row for each parcel. In Splunk, this requires a stats latest() or dedup operation across millions of records, which is computationally heavy and slow.
                                                             ii.      Date filter doesn't reduce the scan size much

Even when filtering by encoded date, Splunk still needs to trace the full history of every parcel from that date — including events that happened days or weeks later — to determine today's current status. The filtered date only narrows which parcels to look at, not how much data to scan.
                                                           iii.      Query performance and timeout risk

A single dashboard query that reconstructs the latest status for ~50,000–80,000 parcels encoded on one day (estimated daily volume) from a pool of millions of rows may exceed Splunk's query timeout limits, or return results so slowly it becomes unusable in a live dashboard.
                                                           iv.      Concurrent usage multiplies the load

If multiple users open the dashboard simultaneously with different date filters, the Splunk cluster will face parallel heavy queries, potentially degrading performance across all other operations that depend on Splunk.
My Recommendation
                                                              i.      Given these constraints, we recommend raising this request through APR and routing it to IT Support. Unlike our current Splunk setup, IT has direct database access where parcel records can be queried relationally and efficiently — making it far more suitable for this type of summary dashboard.

                                                             ii.      With proper database access, IT would be able to build a scalable, performant solution that can handle our data volume without the limitations we face on Splunk. Any development done at that level will also be easier to maintain and extend as our operations grow."
